record_type_quote:
We now have longer time series on more nations and the information about
      happiness in the USA has been enriched with additional time series from the Gallup
      archive (Gallup Brain), recently published by Jones (2004), Saad (2004) and Carroll

targets.title: Feeding the illusion of growth and happiness: A reply to Hagerty and Veenhoven
targets.evidence_quote:
Richard Easterlin elegantly disputed these findings in a paper: Feeding the
      Illusion of Growth and Happiness: A Reply to Hagerty and Veenhoven, published in this
      journal (Easterlin 2005).
targets.outcome_quote:
All in all, it seems that people have become happier in the second half of the 20th century
    and that the gains in happiness have been greater in poor nations than in rich nations.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The extended national survey series contradict the closest target in the debate: Easterlin’s 2005 no-growth interpretation. The overall judgment is rising happiness despite measurement uncertainty.

reasoning: Identity confirmed from title, authors and DOI in complete PDF, including references. New survey waves and additional national series test the previously published no-rise finding, rather than solely re-running its original data. Easterlin 2005 is the closest explicitly disputed target; earlier Easterlin articles describe the chain, and Hagerty and Veenhoven 2003 supplies the position defended here.
